definition.text: Spells are level-based magical effects. Lower-level characters can learn only lower-level spells; higher-level characters can access higher-level spells.
Only special classes can cast spells.

definition.rule: If a rule does not specify arcane or divine, it applies to both.

definition.text: A spellcaster’s available spells are called the spell repertoire.

rules.rule: Per day, a spellcaster may cast the number of spells of each level shown on the Spells Progression table for that class.
Spellcasters do not prepare or memorize specific spells in advance.

At the time of casting, a spellcaster may choose any spell in the spellcaster’s repertoire that is of a level the caster can cast and for which the caster still has an unused daily spell slot of that level.
After all available spells for the day are expended, the caster must have 8 hours of uninterrupted rest and 1 hour of concentrated study or prayer before casting again.
A spellcaster must be able to move hands and speak to cast.
A spellcaster cannot cast while gagged.
A spellcaster cannot cast while hands are tied.
A spellcaster cannot cast while in an area affected by silence.
A spellcaster may take no other actions in the same round the caster intends to cast a spell.
A PC must announce intent to cast before initiative is determined at the beginning of the round.
If the caster takes damage before the spell is cast, the spell is disrupted and fails.
If the caster is required to make a saving throw before the spell is cast and fails it, the spell is disrupted and fails.
A disrupted spell still counts against spells per day as though cast.
Unless otherwise noted, the intended target must be within the caster’s visual range.
The target may be a specific monster, a specific character, or an area of effect.
Divine spellcasters receive spells directly from the deity they serve.
Their repertoire automatically includes each spell of each level they can cast from the spell list made available to them by their deity.
A divine spellcaster does not necessarily have access to every divine spell in existence.
Each day, usually in the morning, a well-rested divine spellcaster must pray for at least 1 hour to be able to cast spells.
The exact divine spells available to a cleric depend on the deity served.
The Judge determines which spells are appropriate for a given cleric based on the deity or power served.
The bladedancer spell list is an example of a deity-specific divine spell list.
Arcane spellcasters have a limited repertoire of spells.
The base number and level of spells in an arcane spellcaster’s repertoire equals the number and level of spells the caster can cast per day.
The number of spells of each level in the repertoire is increased by the caster’s Intelligence bonus.
A formula for each spell in the repertoire is recorded in spell books.
A blank spell book costs 20gp and has 100 pages.
Each spell formula uses 1 page per spell level.
Arcane casters may possess spell formula not currently in repertoire.
Maintaining a spell in repertoire is separate from merely possessing its formula.
Spell formula accumulated over time are used when changing repertoire.

starting_repertoire.rule: A 1st-level arcane spellcaster begins with a base of one 1st-level spell in repertoire.
The Judge selects the initial spell.
If the mage has INT 13 or higher, the mage may begin with additional 1st-level spells up to the Intelligence bonus.

procedure.name: random_additional_starting_spells
procedure.step: For each point of Intelligence bonus, roll 1d12 on the arcane 1st-level spell list.
Add the indicated spell to the repertoire.
If a duplicate is rolled, do not reroll.
The character begins play with fewer than the maximum possible spells if duplicates reduce the total.

rules.rule: Arcane spellcasters add new spells in several ways as they gain levels.
Mages and elven spellswords are assumed to belong to the local mages’ guild or be apprenticed to a higher-level NPC.
When they gain a level, they may return to their masters and be out of play for 1 game week per spell while adding new spells to repertoire.
Their masters teach them spells equal to the number and level of spells the caster can use in a single day.
Characters of 9th level or above do not have masters to teach them spells.
Without a master, mages and elven spellswords must rely on found scrolls, found spell books, or spell research.

procedure.name: add_spell_from_scroll_or_spellbook
procedure.step: Obtain a new spell from a scroll or another arcane spellcaster’s spell book.
Check whether the character can still learn new spells of that spell level.
If the spell level is too high for the character to cast, it cannot enter the repertoire yet, but the formula may be saved for later.
Spend 1 week of study to add the spell to the repertoire.
If the source is a scroll, scribing uses up the scroll.
If the source is a spell book, copying does not erase the original spell.

reading_restrictions.rule: A scroll or spell book can be read only by its creator or by an arcane spellcaster who can read the language it is written in.
Arcane spellcasters may use read languages to read a scroll or spell book written in an unfamiliar language.

rules.rule: If an arcane spellcaster loses access to spell books, the caster’s repertoire deteriorates over time.
Each week without access to spell books, the caster loses 1 spell level from repertoire.
This continues until the caster knows no spells at all.

procedure.name: rewrite_lost_or_destroyed_spellbooks
procedure.step: For each spell to be rewritten, count total spell levels being restored.
Spend 1 week and 1,000gp per spell level.
The character must devote complete concentration to this activity.
The character may not engage in any other activity during this time.

rules.rule: An arcane spellcaster with a full repertoire may replace a known spell with another spell of equal level.
The caster must possess a copy of the new spell’s formula.
Replacing a spell in repertoire does not cause loss of the replaced spell’s formula.

procedure.name: replace_spell_in_repertoire
procedure.step: Choose one spell currently in repertoire.
Choose another spell of equal level for which the caster has the formula.
Spend 1 week and 1,000gp per spell level.
During this time, the caster must engage in no other activity.
At completion, the old spell is removed from repertoire and the new spell is added.

definition.text: Any spell marked with an asterisk (*) on the spell list may be cast in reverse.

rules.rule: A reversed spell produces the opposite effect of the normal spell.
If a spell is not marked with an asterisk, it is not reversible.
Arcane spellcasters treat the normal and reversed versions as separate spells.
In general, divine spellcasters know both the normal and reversed forms of any reversible spell on their spell list.
Lawful divine spellcasters prefer normal forms and use reversed forms only against Chaotic opponents.
Chaotic divine spellcasters freely use reversed forms and use normal forms to aid comrades and followers.
A deity may restrict a divine spellcaster from using normal or reversed forms of particular spells, at Judge discretion.
If the reversed effect is not self-evident, the individual spell description explains it.

definition.text: The distinctive sensory effects associated with a caster’s version of a spell.

rules.rule: Each spellcaster should write a short description of the signature for each spell the caster can cast.
For arcane spellcasters, a spell signature may reflect a school/style of magic or the caster’s personal style.
For divine spellcasters, a spell signature reflects the caster’s relationship with the deity.
A character’s proficiencies may suggest appropriate spell signatures.
Characters with Sensing Power can sense the spell signature of arcane casters for up to 24 hours after a spell has been cast.
Characters with Collegiate Wizard or Theology may identify particular schools or faiths by spell signature on a proficiency throw of 11+.
